Marathon Petroleum has dropped 1.2% today and nearly 19% over the past two weeks, a decline that tracks the stock's fall since early November. The sharp selloff appears tied to the midterm election results: a Democratic sweep in early November shifted the political landscape toward renewable energy investment and away from fossil fuels, which is a structural headwind for a major oil refiner. At the same time, U.S. crude oil prices have softened from around $145 a barrel at the end of October to $99.64 today—a drop that directly squeezes refining margins (the profit refiners make converting crude into gasoline and diesel).

Refineries are running at 94.5% capacity and storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain ample, meaning weak demand and lower oil prices are compressing what refiners can earn on each barrel processed. The political shift toward renewables is a longer-term headwind, but the immediate pressure comes from falling oil prices and soft energy demand that eat directly into the company's bottom line.
